rationale: B is better because its allocation is driven primarily by quantizer-specific, layer-isolation measurements and validated on disjoint text with useful ablations and a negative control. It is also more calibrated about architecture dependence and handles parameter-count budgets more coherently. A is thorough, but incorrectly treats Hessian and Fisher diagonals as equivalent and cheaply obtainable, then claims a parameter-weighted budget while using an equal-size-layer formula. B still has flaws—especially arbitrary thresholds, an inaccurate description of AWQ as retaining channels at 8-bit, and backwards CKA reasoning for protected layers—but its core procedure is more direct and actionable.
